The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Two circles with centres A and B as shown below have radii of 7 cm and 10 cm respectively. If the length of the common chord PQ is 8 cm, what is the length of AB? Show all your work.

[Image: Two intersecting circles with centers A and B]

Figure, described in words:
Two intersecting circles are shown. The smaller circle on the left has its center labeled A, and the larger circle on the right has its center labeled B. A horizontal line segment connects center A and center B. The two circles intersect at two points labeled P (top) and Q (bottom). A vertical line segment connects P and Q, intersecting line segment AB. Line segment AP is drawn and labeled "7 cm", and line segment BP is drawn and labeled "10 cm".

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer:
The perpendicular from each circle’s centre to the common chord bisects the chord, so each half of PQ is 4 cm. Let O be the midpoint of PQ on AB. Then

AO = √(7² − 4²) = √33 cm,
BO = √(10² − 4²) = √84 = 2√21 cm.

As shown, the centres lie on opposite sides of the common chord’s midpoint, so
AB = AO + BO = √33 + 2√21 ≈ 12.34 cm.
